findings.summary: The incorporated lifecycle package does not test or enforce the Exam's legal attribution requirement for a current qualified privacy/legal records owner. `DISPOSITION-AUTHORIZATION.schema.json` and `RAW-POLICY-GRANT.schema.json` contain only a constant `signerRole` plus a local record signature; they omit verified human subject, active hat and current qualification/assignment, identity issuer and immutable evidence, session, server decision time, authorization-policy evidence, and durable provider proof. The semantic oracle manufactures these records with the module's fixed local fixture key and accepts them solely on structure, digest, that key, role string, time window, and object bindings. An independently executed target-bound positive `RC-FAILED-RUN` lifecycle fixture reached `deleted-tombstoned` with `effects.lifecycle=1` even though its authorization record had none of those human identity, authority, session, or provider-proof fields. No declared lifecycle case supplies an unqualified, transferred, revoked, wrong-subject, wrong-hat, identity-evidence-missing, session-invalid, or provider-proof-missing disposition signer. The same gap is visible in the present HR-01-R2 prerequisite: it binds the policy and canonical Exam and preserves the non-authorizing boundary, but it has no verified stable subject, identity issuer/evidence, authorization-policy binding, sequence, or durable provider message ID and is not validated against any closed ruling schema or semantic oracle. Thus the package can claim the qualified-human prerequisite and authorize deletion/crypto-erasure without mechanically proving the human identity and active authority required by A10.1, section 9, A16, and the Gate policy.
findings.requiredResolution: Define one closed, target-bound human-ruling and disposition-authority envelope/schema that carries the complete A10.1 identity, active-hat, qualification/assignment, session, server-time, authorization-policy, provider-record, provider-proof, sequence, policy, target, inventory, hold/reference, and conditions binding. Validate its signature and provider proof against independently selected trust anchors rather than a fixture-local signer or role assertion. Make HR-01-R2 and every raw-policy grant and per-copy disposition authorization pass that same semantic path. Add positive and zero-effect negative cases for wrong, absent, unverified, disabled, transferred, revoked, expired, unqualified, wrong-hat, wrong-session, stale-policy/target, missing identity evidence, missing/invalid provider proof, and replay/race signers. Refresh all affected digests, obtain a new actual qualified-human ruling over the final bytes, and repeat exact-revision independent Legal review; this agent cannot create, infer, or waive that ruling.

findings.summary: The incorporated legal-control package is not executable against the immutable round-three Exam revision. `validate-remediation.mjs` completes its declared signature/authorization, sanitized-real, lifecycle, recovery, cost, and other loops but then asserts that the canonical Exam still has the superseded pre-incorporation SHA-256 `91f2744d0675f3c62eb122b2783e3aee147c85981740d0f3f4409b53808e6b10`; the protected incorporated Exam is `84ad1d4c14d6614fe4b53509104e379e9ad6dff0462c96109901eefb1e02fd7f`. The observed target run therefore terminates with an assertion failure rather than a target-bound pass. A16 and the round-two technical-release predicate require the package schemas and deterministic fixtures to pass at the exact canonical Exam revision, so R10's pre-incorporation PASS cannot substitute for an executable legal record, retention, disposition, signed-log/provider-proof, and signature matrix at this target.
findings.requiredResolution: Provide an exact-revision validator mode that verifies the protected incorporated Exam and all bound legal-control artifacts without expecting the obsolete base Exam digest. It must execute the complete corrected human-ruling and disposition-authority identity/proof matrix, require declared-versus-executed ID equality, and produce a pass bound to the final canonical Exam revision and refreshed package digests before a new independent Legal review.

escalations.reason: LEGAL-G2-R3-001 and LEGAL-G2-R3-002 leave unresolved major attribution, disposition-authority, human-ruling, and exact-revision testability gaps. The commercial default-closed policy requires Legal specialist escalation unless a revised exact target closes them; this agent cannot accept or waive the residual risk.

The exact target has no passing target-bound validator for the legal controls, and the current HR-01-R2 and lifecycle authorization records lack the closed identity, qualification, policy, and durable provider-proof evidence needed to establish the required human authority mechanically.

The Exam and retention policy reserve lifecycle policy acceptance and disposition authority to a current qualified privacy/legal records owner. Closing the record and evidence contract and issuing a new ruling require that qualified human; this agent cannot provide legal advice, declare qualification, or substitute its review for the ruling.

The defective authorization predicate gates deletion and cryptographic erasure of corpus, evidence, provider, history, backup, and export copies. Permitting those irreversible effects without verified current human authority can materially affect originator and records-preservation rights, so no disposition risk is accepted here.
